about: Ground surfaces read off the owner's photographs where the inventory (data/ground.geojson) disagrees. Measured on the ground plane through each photo's SOLVED camera (an orthographic resample, 1 cm a pixel); rings in v2 metres (x east, z south). Photo wins over outline. Drawn last (scripts/v2/ground_near.py).

features.why: Anna Hiss courtyard, package photo-1: the slab in front of the paver band, from the band's end to past the photographer, is one light concrete slab (the inventory and the aerial's green hint drew lawn in its south part). Drawn before the paver band, so the band stays on top.
Anna Hiss courtyard, package photo-1: the band between the two planting beds, from the gym's steps to the concrete slab, is buff brick pavers (the inventory has concrete)

Norman Hackerman Building, package photo-1: the street in front of the building, curb to 9 m out, is asphalt (nothing in the inventory names it and the aerial's tree-shaded colour read as concrete). The curb line is measured through the photo's solved camera; the far side is the street's usual width.

Anna Hiss courtyard, package photo-3: the lawn between the planting beds, the curved concrete planter wall and the walk is lawn (the inventory has a City 'patio' polygon that the bake defaulted to brick pavers, and the 2025 aerial does not read it as green). Outlined on the photo and carried to the ground through the photo's solved camera.
